Subject: Results: MAP perf validation + recommended throttles (see attachments)

Samir / Maya — we ran the test this morning in us-west-2 per the plan. High-level summary first, full artifacts attached.

Summary (one-paragraph): Redwood Dedicated met the MAP targets for steady-state throughput and TTFT; the burst windows triggered transient queueing but no sustained failures. We recommend a conservative gateway-rate-limit for ACME with a per-customer token-bucket and a short burst allowance to avoid immediate 429 cascades.

Key numbers:
- Steady-state: sustained 500 req/s for 30m. Median latency = 210ms; P95 = 320ms; P99 = 540ms. Error rate = 0.14% (network retries during client-side fan-out).
- Burst windows: when we injected 2,000 req/s for 90s the queue depth peaked at ~1.2k requests; queue fully drained in 45s after spike end for quantized variant. No OOMs or worker crashes.
- TTFT (cold streams): median first-token = 98ms; max observed = 170ms (single outlier while a container was spinning up).

Recommended rate-limit (suggested for API Gateway):
- Per-customer token bucket: refill = 500 tokens/minute (~8.3 req/s sustained)
- Burst capacity = 2,500 tokens (allows transient bursts up to ~2k for short windows)
- Graceful 429 policy: return Retry-After 8s and allow client exponential backoff with jitter

Attachments included: performance-results-20260630.csv (per-second metrics), queueing-screens.png (queue depth timeline), one-page procurement-summary.pdf (inline in ACME drive link).

Next steps:
- Procurement: we can attach the one-page PDF to the MAP and mark perf validation complete for ACME-2026-042.
- Ops: if you want, we can run a second test against your on-prem proxy in July to validate network fan-out effects.

Best,
